questions.text: Choose the passive form: "The cat chased the mouse."
questions.explanation: Simple past active → "was/were + past participle".

source.label: Original practice set by Claude, not expert-reviewed

options: The cat was chased by the mouse.
The mouse is chased by the cat.
The mouse was chased by the cat.
The mouse has been chased by the cat.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Choose the passive form: "They are building a new bridge."
questions.explanation: Present continuous active → "is/are being + past participle".

source.label: Original practice set by Claude, not expert-reviewed

options: A new bridge is being built by them.
A new bridge was being built by them.
A new bridge has been built by them.
A new bridge is built by them.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Choose the passive form: "She has finished the work."
questions.explanation: Present perfect active → "has/have been + past participle".

source.label: Original practice set by Claude, not expert-reviewed

options: The work had been finished by her.
The work was finished by her.
The work has been finished by her.
The work is finished by her.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Choose the passive form: "Ravi will write the letter."
questions.explanation: Simple future active → "will be + past participle".

source.label: Original practice set by Claude, not expert-reviewed

options: The letter would be written by Ravi.
The letter is written by Ravi.
The letter will be written by Ravi.
The letter will have written by Ravi.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Choose the passive form: "Who broke the window?"
questions.explanation: Questions with "who" become "By whom + was/were + subject + past participle?".

source.label: Original practice set by Claude, not expert-reviewed

options: By whom the window was broken?
By whom was the window broken?

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Choose the passive form: "Open the door."
questions.explanation: Imperative sentences become "Let + object + be + past participle".

source.label: Original practice set by Claude, not expert-reviewed

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Choose the active form: "The song was sung by Meena."
questions.explanation: "Was sung" is simple past passive, so the active is "sang".

source.label: Original practice set by Claude, not expert-reviewed

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Choose the indirect form: He said, "I am busy."
questions.explanation: After a past reporting verb, "am" changes to "was" and "I" to "he".

source.label: Original practice set by Claude, not expert-reviewed

options: He said that I was busy.
He said that he was busy.
He said that he had been busy.
He said that he is busy.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Choose the indirect form: She said, "I will come tomorrow."
questions.explanation: "Will" becomes "would" and "tomorrow" becomes "the next day".

source.label: Original practice set by Claude, not expert-reviewed

options: She said that I would come the next day.
She said that she would come the next day.
She said that she would come tomorrow.
She said that she will come tomorrow.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Choose the indirect form: He said to me, "Where do you live?"
questions.explanation: A question becomes a statement order, "said to" becomes "asked", and the tense moves back.

source.label: Original practice set by Claude, not expert-reviewed

options: He told me where I lived.
He asked me where I lived.
He asked me where did I live.
He asked me where do I live.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Choose the indirect form: The teacher said, "The earth goes round the sun."
questions.explanation: A universal truth keeps its present tense.

source.label: Original practice set by Claude, not expert-reviewed

options: The teacher said that the earth went round the sun.
The teacher told that the earth goes round the sun.
The teacher said that the earth had gone round the sun.
The teacher said that the earth goes round the sun.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Choose the indirect form: She said to him, "Please help me."
questions.explanation: A polite command becomes "requested + object + to + verb".

source.label: Original practice set by Claude, not expert-reviewed

options: She requested him to help her.
She said him to help her.
She ordered him that he help her.
She requested him to help me.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Choose the indirect form: He said, "I have finished my work."
questions.explanation: "Have finished" becomes "had finished"; pronouns change to "he/his".

source.label: Original practice set by Claude, not expert-reviewed

options: He said that he finished his work.
He said that he has finished his work.
He said that he had finished his work.
He said that I had finished my work.
